g: a todos los santos
a + a personal before a group of people introduces the recipients: ‘to all the saints’.
e: junto con los obispos y diáconos
junto con means ‘together with’ and adds the overseers and deacons to the greeting.

g: Que Dios ... les concedan
Opening Que plus the subjunctive concedan forms a blessing: ‘May God ... grant you’.
e: gracia y paz
A conventional letter greeting: ‘grace and peace’; the two nouns are coordinated without an article.

g: cada vez que me acuerdo
cada vez que introduces a repeated occasion; me acuerdo is first-person present, ‘I remember’.
e: Doy gracias a mi Dios
dar gracias a means ‘give thanks to’; mi Dios makes the reference personal.

g: En todas mis oraciones
The preposition en locates the action within ‘all my prayers’; mis agrees with feminine plural oraciones.
e: oro con alegría
con alegría literally means ‘with joy’ and describes the manner of oro, ‘I pray’.

g: han participado
han + participado is the present perfect, describing participation continuing in relevance to now.
e: desde el primer día hasta ahora
desde ... hasta marks a span: ‘from the first day until now’.

g: la irá perfeccionando
ir + gerund here expresses an ongoing future process: ‘will keep perfecting it’.
e: hasta el día de Cristo Jesús
hasta sets the endpoint of the process: ‘until the day of Christ Jesus’.

g: ya sea que me encuentre preso
ya sea que introduces an alternative and takes subjunctive encuentre: ‘whether I am imprisoned’.
e: los llevo en el corazón
llevar en el corazón is an affectionate idiom: ‘I carry you in my heart’.

g: de cuánto los quiero
cuánto introduces the extent of querer: God is witness to ‘how much I love you’.
e: el entrañable amor
entrañable derives from entrañas, ‘inner parts’, and conveys very deep affection.

g: que el amor de ustedes abunde
The content of pido en oración is introduced by que + subjunctive abunde, expressing Paul’s request.
e: cada vez más
A fixed comparative phrase meaning ‘more and more’; it intensifies abunde.

g: para que disciernan
para que expresses purpose and requires subjunctive disciernan: ‘so that you may discern’.
e: lo que es mejor
lo que is ‘what/that which’ and turns the following clause into the object to discern.

g: llenos del fruto de justicia
llenos is an adjective agreeing with an implied plural group; de introduces what they are filled with.
e: para gloria y alabanza de Dios
para marks the intended result: ‘for God’s glory and praise’.

g: ha contribuido al avance
ha contribuido is present perfect; al contracts a + el before the masculine noun avance.
e: en realidad
An adverbial phrase meaning ‘in fact’ or ‘actually’, used to clarify the situation.

g: se ha hecho evidente
se ha hecho is a present-perfect change-of-state construction: ‘has become evident’.
e: por causa de Cristo
por causa de means ‘because of’ or ‘on account of’ and gives the reason for the chains.

g: se han atrevido a anunciar
atreverse a + infinitive means ‘dare to’; se han atrevido is present perfect plural.
e: sin temor
sin + noun means ‘without’; sin temor describes their fearless manner of announcing.

g: pero otros lo hacen
pero contrasts the first group with otros; lo is the neuter object, ‘it’ (preaching).
e: con buenas intenciones
con buenas intenciones means ‘with good motives’; con introduces the manner or motivation.

g: he sido puesto
he sido puesto is the present perfect passive: ‘I have been appointed/placed’.
e: por amor
por amor means ‘out of love’; por identifies the motive of Estos últimos.

g: creyendo que así van a aumentar
creyendo is a gerund giving their accompanying thought; van a aumentar is a near-future construction.
e: motivos puros
motivos puros means ‘pure motives’; puros agrees with masculine plural motivos.

g: sea como sea
The subjunctive sea in this fixed phrase means ‘however it may be’ or ‘in any case’.
e: Al fin y al cabo
An idiom meaning ‘after all’ or ‘when all is said and done’; it frames Paul’s conclusion.

g: resultará en mi liberación
resultar en means ‘result in’; the future resultará states the expected outcome.
e: gracias a las oraciones de ustedes
gracias a means ‘thanks to’ and credits the readers’ prayers as a means.

g: ya sea que yo viva o muera
ya sea que sets alternatives and takes subjunctives viva and muera: ‘whether I live or die’.
e: Cristo será exaltado en mi cuerpo
The future passive será exaltado means ‘will be exalted’; en mi cuerpo specifies the sphere.

g: el vivir ... el morir
Infinitives can function as nouns; el turns vivir and morir into ‘living’ and ‘dying’.
e: para mí
para mí means ‘for me’ and marks this as Paul’s personal evaluation.

g: si seguir viviendo ... representa
The whole infinitive phrase seguir viviendo is the subject of singular representa after si, ‘if continuing to live means’.
e: ¡No lo sé!
lo is a neuter pronoun referring to the choice; the phrase means ‘I do not know it’.

g: deseo partir y estar
deseo is followed by two coordinated infinitives, partir and estar, expressing what he wants.
e: muchísimo mejor
muchísimo intensifies mejor: ‘very much better’ or ‘far better’.

g: es preferible que yo permanezca
es preferible que requires subjunctive permanezca because it evaluates a desired alternative.
e: por el bien de ustedes
por el bien de means ‘for the good of’; it states whose benefit is in view.

g: sé que permaneceré y continuaré
sé que introduces future indicatives permaneceré and continuaré, expressing a settled expectation.
e: avance en la fe
avance means ‘progress’; en la fe identifies the area in which that progress occurs.

g: cuando yo vuelva
A future time clause uses present subjunctive vuelva after cuando: ‘when I return’.
e: por causa mía
por causa de + possessive means ‘because of me’; mía agrees with the understood feminine causa.

g: Pase lo que pase
Pase is subjunctive in an open-ended concessive phrase: ‘whatever happens’.
e: de una manera digna
de una manera digna means ‘in a manner worthy’; digna agrees with feminine manera.

g: lo cual es para ellos señal
lo cual refers back to the preceding situation as a whole, not to one noun.
e: en cambio
A discourse connector meaning ‘by contrast’ or ‘on the other hand’.

g: se les ha concedido
An impersonal passive-like construction: les identifies those to whom something ‘has been granted’.
e: no solo creer en Cristo, sino también sufrir por él
no solo ... sino también pairs two infinitives: ‘not only to believe ... but also to suffer’.

g: que antes me vieron sostener
ver + infinitive lets vieron express ‘saw’ while sostener names the action seen.
e: la misma lucha
misma means ‘same’ and links the readers’ struggle with Paul’s earlier one.
